newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SICOM rubber futures volume surges on baht fall.
newsitem.headline: SICOM rubber futures volume surges on baht fall.

text.p: Futures trading in the Singapore Commodity Exchange's (SICOM) four main rubber contracts was the second highest on record on July 2, following the sharp fall in the Thai baht after its flotation, SICOM said on Thursday.
Thai rubber producers were major sellers in the market and were met by buyers in the shape of fund managers who were bargain hunting, the exchange said in a statement.
The total rubber volume traded on SICOM on July 2 was 36,555 tonnes, comprising 4,150 tonnes of RSS1, 14,525 tonnes of RSS3, 660 tonnes of TSR20 Award and 17,220 tonnes of TSR20 FOB.
This was the second highest daily volume on the exchange since August 23, 1995 when 42,455 tonnes of rubber traded.
Singapore rubber futures prices plunged on Wednesday with the August RSS3 contract shedding 7.50 U.S. cents to hit 92 cents a kg. Around midday on Thursday SICOM rubber was untraded.
